question: Does the Lil Nouns NFT contract report a totalSupply() of at least 8,000 at the closing block of the pinned window?

definitions.call: totalSupply() with no arguments, returning uint256, read with eth_call at the closing block of the pinned window
definitions.contract: Lil Nouns at 0x4b10701bfd7bfedc47d50562b76b436fbb5bdb3b on Ethereum mainnet
definitions.comparison: true if the returned value is greater than or equal to 8000, otherwise false

answer.notes: Computed with eth_call of selector 0x18160ddd (totalSupply()) against 0x4b10701bfd7bfedc47d50562b76b436fbb5bdb3b at block 0x18d0e5b (26021467), the pinned closing block. Result: 0x...1e08 = 7688. 7688 >= 8000 is false, so the answer is false and the figure behind it is 7688. Endpoints used, three distinct operators, each first checked with eth_chainId (0x1) and eth_getBlockByNumber(26021467) against the pinned closing hash, which matched on all of them: https://one.valve.city/rpc/vk_demo/evm/1, https://eth-mainnet.nodereal.io/v1/1659dfb40aa24bbb8153a677b98064d7 and https://virginia.rpc.blxrbdn.com. All three returned 7688 for the call. Two further endpoints from the row were tried and dropped without being counted: https://rpc.flashbots.net/fast confirmed the chain id and both window block hashes but answers eth_call with HTTP 403, and https://rpc.mevblocker.io/fast and https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com returned HTTP 403 to every request from this machine. Cross-checked independently with `cast call ... --block 26021467` on two of the three working endpoints, which also returned 7688 and confirmed name()="LilNoun", symbol()="LILNOUN". The chain head at read time was 26021566, so the closing block was 99 blocks back and within the non-archive state window of ordinary nodes; no archive node or indexer was needed and no eth_getLogs scan was involved. This question fits the catalogue's call-compare recipe exactly, so no approximation was made: the recipe reproduces the answer from public RPC data alone.
